study_identification.title: Normative modeling of brain morphometry in self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes

study_characteristics.study_objective: Quantify individual deviations from normative ranges of regional brain morphometry in children with SeLECTS and assess associations with clinical manifestations and cognition using sex-specific normative models trained on typically developing children.

dataset_name.answer: devCCNP (Chinese Color Nest Project; CKG; PEK)
dataset_name.reason: Training data for normative models comprised two devCCNP center samples (CKG, PEK).
dataset_name.supporting_text: The data for model training consists of two samples: the CKG sample and the PEK sample... both sourced from the developing Chinese Color Nest Project (devCCNP).

hc_n.supporting_text: data from a multisite sample of 457 healthy individuals (47.3% female; aged 3 to 18 years) from the devCCNP.

deviation_metric.answer: Z-scores; infra-normal if z<-1.96; supra-normal if z>1.96; percentages by region and counts across regions
deviation_metric.reason: Deviation defined via z-scores relative to normative mean and variance; thresholds at ±1.96.
deviation_metric.supporting_text: The normative deviation for each regional morphometric measure was defined as the z‑scores ... we defined regional non‑normal z‑scores as infra‑normal when they fell below −1.96 or supra‑normal when they exceeded 1.96 ...

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Two‑proportion z‑tests for percentages; two‑sample t‑tests for z‑scores and observed measures; Spearman correlations (counts of abnormal regions vs. clinical variables); Pearson correlations (averaged deviations vs. clinical variables); 5‑fold cross‑validated linear SVC (scikit‑learn v1.2.2) to classify SeLECTS vs HC using deviation vs observed features; FDR correction applied.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Children with SeLECTS showed more infra‑normal subcortical volume deviations than controls; counts of abnormal regions correlated with disease duration, seizure frequency, and Raven’s score, while average deviations largely overlapped between groups.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Among SeLECTS (n=187), infra‑normal deviations observed in 34.2% (subcortical volume), 86.1% (cortical thickness), 82.4% (surface area); controls (n=108): 18.5%, 77.8%, 74.1%. Supra‑normal: SeLECTS 35.8%/80.7%/91.4% vs controls 27.8%/78.7%/88.9%. Subcortical infra‑normal counts higher in SeLECTS across areas (χ2=7.54, P=0.04 FDR). Averaged z‑score distributions nearly overlapped; only 1 SeLECTS case showed averaged supra‑normal surface area. Associations: supra‑normal subcortical count with disease duration (R2=0.06, P=0.05) and seizure frequency (R2=0.11, P=0.01); infra‑normal cortical thickness count with Raven’s total (R2=0.07, P=0.05).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Limited sample size for more stable/generalizable models; cross‑sectional morphometry (no longitudinal trajectories) may underestimate age effects; models included only sex and age, omitting other demographic/developmental/lifestyle factors.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Normative models were sex‑specific and region‑wise; global covariates (ICV/mean CT/mean SA) improved performance; used functional gradient analyses; compared deviation‑based vs observed‑measure SVC classification with 5‑fold CV.

general_notes.general_notes: Supplementary material is stated as available at Cerebral Cortex online (suggesting journal). Training cohort came from devCCNP centers (CKG, PEK); site handled via ComBat‑GAM; text also mentions treating site as a random factor, but no hierarchical model is described. No explicit QC thresholds reported.
